subject: Post-call: SLO checklist + multi-region routing & residency clarifications
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sara Thompson <sara@finlytics.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: SLOs, routing, and data residency (FinLytics)

Hi Sara — great to meet earlier.  Quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can scope a focused perf POC: 

What we heard from FinLytics on the call:
- Target p95 end-to-end generation latency for typical interactive prompts: US < 150ms, EU < 200ms, APAC < 300ms.
- Sustained concurrency target: 500 concurrent requests; peak burst to ~1,500.
- Streaming required: partial token delivery/streaming for UI snappiness (user requirement: first token within ~50ms of compute start).
- Throughput goal: ~120 requests/sec sustained during business hours; up to 400 rps during peak events.
- Data residency: all EU customer data must remain in EU region (including logs and KV cache); APAC data must stay within APAC region; US data may use multi-AZ US regions.
- Security: SOC2 evidence and audit logs are required for procurement.

Open clarifying questions for your team (if you can confirm in reply):
1) Typical prompt + completion length (avg tokens in / out) and distribution (p50/p95). This drives batching and memory/kv cache sizing.
2) Percent of requests that expect streaming vs fire-and-forget.
3) Tolerance for model variant fallbacks (e.g., quantized smaller model during capacity pressure) — are fallbacks acceptable with explicit degradation?
4) Any hard SLA window for failover between regions (e.g., 30s)?

Next steps we propose:
- Dev perf deep-dive (60m) with Dev and Rafael to size a POC and identify required infra config (suggest Tue 24th or Wed 25th).
- FinLytics to share a sample workload (anonymized) — we referenced finlytics_workload_sample.csv attached.
- Redwood to deliver SLO template and a proposed mutual action plan (attached).

Attachments: redwood_slo_template.pdf, mutual_action_plan_v1.xlsx, finlytics_workload_sample.csv

I’ll loop Rafael and Dev to weigh in on feasibility and scheduling. Thanks — Stephanie

--
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0192
From: Sara Thompson <sara@finlytics.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: FinLytics Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: SLOs, routing, and data residency (FinLytics)

Thanks for the clear summary, Stephanie — that matches what we discussed. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Prompt & response sizes: median ~60 tokens in, ~120 tokens out; p95 closer to 800 tokens total for a small subset of analytic workflows.
- Streaming: ~70% of interactive flows must stream partial tokens to our UI. We expect the SDK to deliver partial tokens as they are produced; target for perceived latency is first partial within 40–60ms.
- Fallbacks: acceptable but only if explicitly labeled to the end user and if latency impact is minimal. Full downgrade to significantly lower-quality models is a last resort.
- Residency: EU production customer traffic must stay in eu-west region; backups to a separate EU region OK for failover but logs/audit trails must remain in EU.

Procurement note: our procurement team would like a SOC2 report and a redline-ready PO/contract. We’re targeting an internal decision by end-April if POC aligns.

Can we confirm Rafael and Dev can join a technical deep-dive on Tue 24 Mar 10:00–11:00 PT (13:00–14:00 ET)?

Thanks,
Sara

Sara Thompson
Head of Product Integrations | FinLytics
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Thompson <sara@finlytics.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 07:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: SLOs, routing, and data residency (FinLytics)

Hi Sara — thanks for the detail. A few technical notes and asks ahead of the deep-dive so we can prepare concrete perf targets and a POC plan: 

1) Workload shaping: please confirm distribution of short vs long requests (we saw median/ p95 above but would benefit from a histogram). Long-tail (800 tokens) impacts memory and KV cache behavior; we may propose different routing/batching for long jobs.
2) Streaming expectations: Redwood supports streaming over HTTP chunked or SSE; we can guarantee sub-60ms first-byte for compute-started responses in the US under our Dedicated profiles for typical prompt sizes. For APAC and EU, latency will depend on regional egress and peering — we’ll validate during POC.
3) Concurrency/throughput sizing: To hit sustained 120 rps and 500 concurrent with p95 targets we’ll likely recommend a Dedicated pool with autoscale and a regional routing policy (US/EU/APAC split) plus an edge routing layer to minimize cross-region hops.
4) Fallback policies: we can expose per-route policies that fall back to a smaller model variant with explicit response metadata. We recommend a canary period to validate quality delta.

Proposed POC steps (we will bring an infra config + test harness):
- Week 1: perf sizing + smoke tests on synthetic workload (we will run in-region).
- Week 2: run scaled load (sustained + burst) with streaming enabled and collect p50/p95/p99.
- Week 3: iterate on batching/kv cache/quantization knobs and re-run.

Please upload a small sample histogram and any SLA language procurement expects to the Drive link so Rafael and I can prepare. Can confirm Tue 24 Mar 10:00 PT works for Rafael and me.

--
Dev Patel
Senior Systems Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Sara Thompson <sara@finlytics.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, FinLytics Procurement <procurement@finlytics.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: SLOs, routing, and data residency (FinLytics) — Next steps

Thanks everyone — quick action list to keep momentum: 

Action items (owners & due dates):
- FinLytics: upload anonymized workload histogram + confirm percent streaming vs non-streaming (owner: Sara) — due Thu 26 Mar EOD.
- Redwood (Dev/Rafael): prepare perf harness + initial Dedicated pool config and run baseline smoke tests (owner: Dev) — begin Wed 25 Mar.
- Stephanie: send SLO template and mutual action plan (done — attachments).
- Procurement (FinLytics): share SOC2 report request and any contract redlines to procurement@redwood.com — target Mon 29 Mar.
- Schedule: Technical deep-dive Tue 24 Mar 10:00 PT (confirmed).

Measurement & success criteria for POC:
- p95 latency: US < 150ms, EU < 200ms, APAC < 300ms for median workloads (verified under 120 rps sustained).
- Streaming: 70% of flows must present first partial token < 60ms after compute start in-region.
- Residency: EU traffic + logs remain in EU; documented in runbook and validated in POC.

I attached the SLO template and a mutual action plan for signature. Rafael/Dev — please add any technical caveats in the Drive doc. Sara — we’ll follow up after the deep-dive with a proposed Dedicated sizing and a one-week perf window.

If there are any timing conflicts or procurement items we should know about, flag them in a quick reply. Looking forward to moving this to POC.

Best,
Stephanie

Attachments: redwood_slo_template.pdf, mutual_action_plan_v1.xlsx, finlytics_workload_sample.csv
